outcome: admission to special care newborn unit
cohort: 120 macrosomic (≥4000 g) newborn and their mothers, and 120 normal weight (2500-3999 g) newborns and their mothers, delivered at three large hospitals in Abuja, Nigeria
finding: Macrosomia was significantly associated with higher rates of birth injuries, perinatal asphyxia, admissions into the special care newborn unit, and hypoglycemia.
mod_finding: The most frequent route of delivery for macrosomic infants was emergency cesarean section, accounting for 42% of births.
birth_weight: macrosomic (birth weight ≥4000 g), normal weight (2500-3999 g)
